$comment: files.list -> GET /drive/v3/files, response FileList. Read from the Drive v3 discovery document 2026-09-30. Scope stays drive.file, which the existing folder_create action already chose over broad drive -- so this only ever lists files the connected app itself created or that the user explicitly opened via a Drive picker, never the whole of My Drive. That is a real, sharp limitation and is said plainly in the description rather than left for someone to discover the first time a file they expected is simply absent from the results.
title: List Google Drive files
description: List files this app created (or the user explicitly opened) in Google Drive. Under the drive.file scope this connector uses, a file created by any other app or picked up in the Drive UI directly never appears here.

query.$comment: Drive v3 returns only id, name and mimeType by default -- everything else has to be asked for explicitly with `fields`, or it is silently absent rather than null. A fixed literal, not a config choice: an author should not have to know Drive's partial-response syntax to get a usable list. Kept lean on purpose -- parents, createdTime and webContentLink are on file_get's fuller projection; a list row is for identifying and previewing, not a full record per file.

config.label: Search query
config.description: Drive's query syntax, e.g. "mimeType='application/pdf' and trashed=false". Leave blank to list everything this app can see.

config.label: Page size
config.description: Files per page. Drive's maximum is 1000.

config.label: Order by
config.description: A comma-separated list of Drive sort keys, e.g. "modifiedTime desc". Leave blank for Drive's default order.

outputShape.description: id, name, mimeType, size, modifiedTime, webViewLink per file -- leaner than file_get's projection. Read one file directly with file_get for parents and webContentLink.
Present when there is another page.
